title: decode_limited: is_truncated=true for exact-limit complete block
description:
Trigger: call decode_limited(b'begin 644 f
#0V%T
 
end
', Some(3)). The block is structurally complete (3 bytes, has terminator and end). Expected: is_truncated=false. Actual: is_truncated=true. Cause: the limit check (data.len() >= max) fires at the start of the loop iteration for the terminator line, before decode_line is called on the ' ' terminator line. So decode_line never processes the terminator, the 'end' lookahead never runs, and is_truncated remains at its initial true value. The data is complete and correct (no data loss), but is_truncated=true causes callers doing preview to believe there are more bytes when there aren't, triggering a redundant full re-fetch. Affects any caller that uses is_truncated to decide whether to fetch more bytes after a max_bytes-bounded preview query.
close_reason: Fixed: changed >= to > in limit check so terminator line is processed when data.len()==max. Added 5 regression tests.
